questions.question_description: Implement a Queue using a fixed-size array. Support the following operations: enqueue (insert at rear), dequeue (remove from front), and display (print all elements from front to rear).
questions.input_format: Integer S (size of queue) and N (number of operations), followed by N lines of commands: 'enqueue X', 'dequeue', 'display'.
questions.output_format: For 'dequeue', print the removed element. Print 'Queue is Full' on overflow, 'Queue is Empty' on underflow. For 'display', print space-separated elements or 'Empty'.
questions.constraints: 1 <= S <= 100. 1 <= N <= 1000. Data values within integer limits.
questions.hints: Use front and rear indices. Enqueue increments rear and inserts. Dequeue increments front. The queue is full when rear == S-1 and empty when front > rear.

test_cases.input:
3 6
enqueue 7
enqueue 8
enqueue 9
dequeue
dequeue
display

questions.solution_explanation: A linear queue uses front and rear indices. Enqueue inserts at rear+1 if not full (rear < S-1). Dequeue removes from front by incrementing front. The queue is empty when front > rear. This approach is simple but wastes space after dequeues since front only moves forward.

questions.question_description: Implement a Queue using a Singly Linked List. Support the following operations: enqueue (insert at rear), dequeue (remove from front), front (peek at front element), and display (print all elements).
questions.input_format: Integer N (number of operations), followed by N lines of commands: 'enqueue X', 'dequeue', 'front', 'display'.
questions.output_format: For 'dequeue', print the removed element. For 'front', print the front element. Print 'Underflow' on dequeue from empty queue. Print 'Empty' for front/display on empty queue. For 'display', print space-separated elements.
questions.constraints: 1 <= N <= 1000. Data values within integer limits.
questions.hints: Maintain front and rear pointers. Enqueue creates a new node at rear. Dequeue removes the node at front. Both are O(1) operations with proper pointer tracking.

test_cases.input:
6
enqueue 42
enqueue 55
dequeue
enqueue 77
front
display

questions.solution_explanation: A linked list queue uses front and rear pointers. Enqueue appends at rear->next in O(1). Dequeue removes the front node in O(1) by advancing the front pointer. When the last element is dequeued, both front and rear must be set to NULL.

questions.question_description: Implement a Circular Queue using a fixed-size array. Support operations: enqueue, dequeue, and display. Handle wrap-around using modulo arithmetic so that dequeued positions can be reused.
questions.input_format: Integer S (size of queue) and N (number of operations), followed by N lines of commands: 'enqueue X', 'dequeue', 'display'.
questions.output_format: For 'dequeue', print the removed element. Print 'Queue is Full' on overflow, 'Queue is Empty' on underflow. For 'display', print space-separated elements from front to rear, or 'Empty'.
questions.hints: Use front and rear initially set to -1. Next position is (rear + 1) % S. The queue is full when (rear + 1) % S == front. When the last element is dequeued, reset both to -1.

enqueue 2
enqueue 3
dequeue
enqueue 4

enqueue 3
dequeue

1

questions.solution_explanation: Circular Queue uses modulo arithmetic to wrap rear and front around the array. This reuses space freed by dequeue operations. Full condition is (rear+1)%S == front. Empty is when front == -1. After dequeuing the last element, both front and rear reset to -1.

questions.question_description: Implement a Circular Queue using a Singly Linked List. Support operations: enqueue (insert at rear), dequeue (remove from front), and display (print all elements). In a circular linked list queue, the rear node's next pointer points back to the front node.
questions.input_format: Integer N (number of operations), followed by N lines of commands: 'enqueue X', 'dequeue', 'display'.
questions.output_format: For 'dequeue', print the removed element. Print 'Underflow' on dequeue from empty queue. For 'display', print space-separated elements, or 'Empty'.
questions.constraints: 1 <= N <= 1000. Data values within integer limits.
questions.hints: Maintain front and rear pointers. When enqueueing the first element, it points to itself. For subsequent enqueues, new node points to front, and old rear points to new node. On dequeue, update rear->next to the new front.

test_cases.input:
6
enqueue 100
enqueue 200
dequeue
enqueue 300
dequeue
display

7
enqueue 1
enqueue 2
enqueue 3
dequeue
dequeue
dequeue
dequeue

questions.solution_explanation: In a Circular Queue implemented with a Linked List, the `next` pointer of the `rear` node always points back to the `front` node, forming a circle. Enqueue involves creating a node, linking `rear->next` to it, and making it point to `front`. Dequeue involves moving `front` to `front->next` and updating `rear->next` to the new `front`. When the last node is dequeued, both pointers become NULL.

questions.question_description: Implement a Priority Queue using an array where each element has a data value and a priority. The element with the highest priority (lowest priority number) is dequeued first. If two elements have the same priority, the one inserted first is dequeued first (FIFO within same priority).
questions.input_format: Integer N (number of operations), followed by N lines of commands: 'enqueue X P' (insert value X with priority P), 'dequeue' (remove highest priority element), 'display' (print all elements).
questions.output_format: For 'dequeue', print the removed value and its priority as 'X P'. Print 'Underflow' if queue is empty. For 'display', print each element as 'X(P)' space-separated in insertion order, or 'Empty'.
questions.constraints: 1 <= N <= 1000. Priority values are positive integers. Lower number = higher priority.
questions.hints: Store data and priority in parallel arrays. When dequeuing, scan the entire array to find the element with the lowest priority number (highest priority). For ties, pick the one with the smallest index.

enqueue 200 1
enqueue 300 2
dequeue
dequeue
display

enqueue 2 2
enqueue 3 1
dequeue

dequeue
dequeue

enqueue 60 1
enqueue 70 3
dequeue
enqueue 80 1
dequeue

questions.solution_explanation: Priority Queue stores elements with associated priorities. On dequeue, it scans the entire array to find the element with the lowest priority number (highest priority). For equal priorities, the element inserted first (lowest index) is chosen, preserving FIFO order. Dequeue shifts remaining elements left to fill the gap. Enqueue is O(1), dequeue is O(N).
